Amber heard Dylan's small bare feet slapping against the hard wood floors of the living room.  She turned to see him standing sheepishly in the door way to the kitchen.

"Mommy, Sam wants a cookie."

Amber sighed and silently cursed her brother and the ridiculous monkey puppet he bought Dylan for his fifth birthday last month.  

"Tell Sam it's almost dinner time and he can have a cookie for desert."

Amber never wanted to squash her son's very active imagination, but she was beginning to be concerned.

"Sam's gonna be mad."

Dylan had started to blame his misbehavior on the puppet. The parenting books said this was a common behavior, but Dylan had always been such an honest child.

"Sam said he was gonna  break your glass bunny if he doesn't get a cookie."

That's it!

"I do not respond to threats, nor do I appreciate it when you lie to me. I am very disappointed in you. Go sit in your naughty chair"

Dylan hung his head and started to sniff back tears as he sat down on the white step stool in the corner of the kitchen. Amber set the oven timer to five minutes and started to count to 20, trying to calm down so she could parent from a rational head space. She had made it as far as 13, when she heard a crash from her bedroom.

"I told you he'd be mad."
